tone_statements.citation: Kandybowicz, Jason. 2026. Absence of Relative Clause Islands in Adara. Languages 11(2): 27. Basel: MDPI.
tone_statements.quote: Data are presented in IPA. Abbreviations for glosses follow the Leipzig Glossing Rules. The following diacritics are used to mark surface tone: V́ = high, V̀ = low, V = mid; V̂ = falling; V̌ = rising. [...] When an embedded verb agrees with a local subject, a special intonation (greater intensity/amplitude on the subject, though no tone change) is required. No special intonation is required when a verb agrees with a non-local subject.
tone_statements.locator: Notes, note 1, p. 9 of 10; sec. on long-distance agreement, p. 6 of 10
tone_statements.n_tones: 3 level (H, M, L) + falling, rising (transcription convention)

tone_statements.quote: The data and judgments presented in this paper come exclusively from fieldwork with the third author, a native speaker of Ekhwa Adara, in the context of a Field Methods class at the CUNY Graduate Center in Fall 2022. Data are presented in IPA. The following diacritics are used to mark surface tone: V́ = high, V̀ = low, V = mid; V̂ = falling, V̌ = rising. [...] Note that the constituent focus particle variant ko, which bears a mid tone, is tonally (not segmentally) contrastive with the high tone-bearing initial interrogative particle kó.

sources.citation: Decker, Ken, Christina Riepe & Longdi Sylvanus. 2024. A Sociolinguistic Survey of the Ejuele (Doka) [dbi] Language of Kaduna State, Nigeria, with Notes on Ikulu. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2024-004, 1-68 (revision of JLSR 2022-025).
sources.note: The only post-2018 descriptive item Glottolog lists for ikv (pp.20-22 concern Ekhwa); SIL survey reports sometimes include a short phonological/tone note with the wordlist. Low odds of a stress statement but it is the last unchecked Glottolog ref.

sources.citation: Bawa, Emmanuel, Rachel Steindel Burdin & Taylor Cassiani. 2023. Cross-linguistic influence in the mid-vowels of Hausa/Ekhwa speakers. In Skarnitzl & Volín (eds.), Proceedings of ICPhS 2023, Prague, 2830-2834. (Glottolog ref 689987)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Vowel-acoustics study; §1.4 says Ekhwa 'has had minimal descriptive linguistic work'; §2.1 (p.2831) says the 32 Ekhwa target words were chosen 'with both low and high tone where possible', and a loanword is transcribed [ɔ̄kɔ́fâ] 'door' — implies a tone system but gives no statement about stress or accent placement.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2020. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, 2020 edition (11 September 2020). Cambridge: ms.
sources.note: Nothing. Entry 111 'Ekhwa' ([Iku]-Gora-Ankwa; autonym ékhwá, sg. énéjì pl. ánárè, tone-marked): sources Maikarfi (2007), Hon et al (2011); Refs: Wordlists: Blench (2009). No phonological statement.

sources.citation: Hon, Luther, Grace Ajaegbu, Carol Magnusson, Uche S. Nweke & Zachariah Yoder. 2018. A Sociolinguistic Survey of the Adara of Kaduna and Niger States, Nigeria. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2018-004. Dallas: SIL International, 78 pp. (Glottolog ref 578992)
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic survey (intelligibility, vitality) with IPA wordlists in appendices (Appendix B: Ankwa/Ekhwa, two villages, 2011); wordlists are not tone-marked; only remark is that the Adara/Ada/Eneje dialects differ by 'lexical and phonological variations' (p.12). No stress, tone or accent statement.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2016. The Ehwa language of Central Nigeria. ms. (revised version cited in Blench 2020 Atlas bibliography)
sources.note: Later revision of the 2009 wordlist we read; if Blench added tone-marked data or a phonology sketch it would supersede the 2009 draft. Live site rogerblench.info returns a JS challenge by automated download; only the 2009 Internet Archive copy was obtainable.

sources.citation: Hon, Luther, Grace Ajaegbu, Carol Magnusson, Uche S. Nweke & Zachariah Yoder. 2012. A Summary of a Sociolinguistic Survey of the Adara of Kaduna and Niger States, Nigeria. SIL, v+18 pp.
sources.note: Summary of the 2018 report already read (which has no phonology); listed only for completeness — very unlikely to add a stress statement.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2009. The E̱hwa language of Central Nigeria. Draft ms. circulated for comment, 5 July 2009, 10 pp. (Glottolog ref 106634)
sources.note: Nothing. Orthographic wordlist collected by Alex Maikarfi; p.2: 'It does not seem worth attempting an analysis of the phonology in the light of these difficulties.' Ehwa forms carry no tone marks; no stress, tone or accent statement anywhere.
sources.venue: Draft ms. circulated for comment, 5 July 2009, 10 pp. (Glottolog ref 106634)

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2006. The Kulu language of Central Nigeria and its affinities. Draft ms., 33 pp. (same web directory)
sources.note: Checked for identity only: this is Ikulu [ikl] (ikul1239), a different language; §3.3 'Kulu has three level tones and at least two glide tones'; nothing about Ehwa/ikv. Not saved under ikug1238.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. [2004; Revision VI, c.2009-10]. Recent research on the Plateau languages of Central Nigeria (web filename 'Plateau State of the '). Draft ms., 23 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. §2.2.1 Northwest Plateau (p.9): 'No new data has been published since this group was set up'; Ẹhwa corresponds to the Iku-Gora-Ankwe cluster and 'clearly deserve[s] separate language status'. Bibliographic overview only.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page for ikug1238 and Wikipedia 'Iku language'

sources.note: Not a tone study, but the first published source with systematically tone-marked Ekhwa data and explicit statements: all examples are transcribed with surface tone using five marks - high, low, mid (unmarked), falling, rising - i.e. three level heights plus two contours; fn.9 states a lexical/grammatical tonal minimal contrast (focus particle ko with mid tone vs interrogative particle kó with high tone, 'tonally (not segmentally) contrastive'); §2 describes polar-question prosody: final-vowel lengthening plus an L% boundary tone, under which phrase-final H and M tones surface as falls while f…
